description: A running sub-agent whose transcript has not moved for five minutes is marked stalled: its age in the control center and in the sub-agent list turns amber and reads "stalled Nm", and the listing carries a subagents_stalled count. A sub-agent that is waiting on purpose, holding an armed Monitor inside its deadline, is never stalled, and when the launch ledger cannot be read nothing is marked. Once a stall passes fifteen minutes the app raises one notification per stall, filed under the parent session, with the per-session mute and the per-type switch honored; an agent that writes again and later stalls again is a new stall. Both limits are named constants (STALL_AFTER, STALL_NOTIFY_AFTER in src/core/subagents/stall.py). Nothing is stopped and no timer is added: the mark rides the watcher's own subagent tally and is pushed through the listing.
examples: A builder sub-agent freezes at 21m 35s: after five quiet minutes its age reads stalled 5m in amber, and at fifteen minutes one notification names the stuck agent in the parent session.
how_to: Open the session control center (click the agents count on the terminal foot bar) or a session's sub-agent list.
Find a running sub-agent whose age reads stalled Nm in amber.
Turn the sub-agent stalled type off or mute the session in settings, notifications, if you do not want the notification.
media_exempt: needs a real sub-agent frozen for five minutes; the amber word is covered by the style guide entry and a unit test, and a recapture recipe needs a fake transcript clock the capture harness does not have
name: Stalled sub-agents
summary: A sub-agent that stops writing turns amber and says stalled, then tells you once.
where: Session control center, agents section: the age cell of a running sub-agent reads stalled Nm in amber.
Sub-agent list popup: the same word in the age column.
Notifications: a sub-agent stalled card, filed under the parent session.
